source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Chapter 6 (PDF 119-138), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 6 (Heat and Thermodynamics) ke poore chapter se practice MCQs hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah; numerical sawalon mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.
6.1 Assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases

blocks.prompt:
1 Thermodynamics is the branch of physics that deals with:
(Thermodynamics physics ki woh shaakh hai jo kis cheez se mutaliq hai?)

options.text: heat aur energy ki doosri shaklon ke darmiyan taalluq aur tabdeeli

blocks.explanation: Thermodynamics heat (hararat) aur energy ki doosri shaklon ke aapas ke taalluq aur tabdeeli se mutaliq hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: deals with the relationships and conversions between heat and other forms of energy

blocks.prompt:
2 Thermodynamics plays a key role in technology because almost all the raw energy available for our use is liberated as:
(Thermodynamics technology mein aham hai kyunke hamare istemal ki taqreeban saari kham (raw) energy kis shakal mein nikalti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Hamare istemal ki taqreeban saari kham energy heat ki shakal mein nikalti hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: almost all the raw energy available for our use is liberated in the form of heat

blocks.prompt:
3 The kinetic theory of gases explains the behaviour of gases on the basis of:
(Kinetic theory of gases gas ke rawayye ki wazahat kis buniyad par karti hai?)

options.text: har molecule ke andar chemical bonds

blocks.explanation: Kinetic theory gas ke rawayye ko us ke zarraat (particles) ki harkat ki buniyad par samjhati hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: explains the behaviour of gases based on the motion of their constituent particles

blocks.prompt:
4 According to the kinetic theory, between collisions gas molecules move:
(Kinetic theory ke mutabiq do takkaron ke darmiyan gas ke molecules kaise harkat karte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Gas ke molecules musalsal be-tarteeb (random) harkat mein hain aur takkar tak seedhi lakeer mein chalte hain (6.1).

book_ref.quote: They move in straight lines until they collide

blocks.prompt:
5 In the kinetic theory, gas particles are treated as point masses because:
(Kinetic theory mein gas ke zarraat ko point masses kyun samjha jata hai?)

options.text: un ka volume gas ke kul volume ke muqable mein na-qabil-e-lehaaz (negligible) hai
woh aapas mein kabhi nahi takrate
woh aik doosre ko zor se kheenchte hain

blocks.explanation: Alag alag molecules ka volume gas ke kul volume ke muqable mein na-qabil-e-lehaaz hai, is liye woh point masses hain (6.1).

book_ref.quote: the particles are considered point masses with no significant volume

blocks.prompt:
6 According to the kinetic theory, ideal gas molecules exert forces on each other:
(Kinetic theory ke mutabiq ideal gas ke molecules aik doosre par force kab lagate hain?)
blocks.explanation: Molecules ke darmiyan koi kashish ya dhakka (repulsion) nahi hota siwaye takkar ke waqt (6.1).

book_ref.quote: The particles do not exert any force on each other except during collisions

blocks.prompt:
7 Collisions of gas molecules with each other and with the walls are perfectly elastic. This means:
(Gas molecules ki aapas mein aur deewaron se takkar perfectly elastic hai. Is ka matlab hai:)

options.text: molecules takkar ke baad chipak jaate hain
saari kinetic energy heat ban jaati hai
kinetic energy ka koi kul nuqsan nahi hota

blocks.explanation: Perfectly elastic takkar mein kinetic energy ka koi kul nuqsan nahi hota; kul kinetic energy mehfooz (conserved) rehti hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: there is no net loss of kinetic energy during collisions

blocks.prompt:
8 The very large number of particles in a gas allows us to describe its properties using:
(Gas mein zarraat ki bohat bari tadaad ki wajah se us ki khususiyaat kis tareeqe se bayan ki ja sakti hain?)

options.text: sirf aik chune hue molecule ki harkat
sirf Newton ka gravitation ka qanoon

blocks.explanation: Gas mein bohat zyada zarraat hote hain, is liye statistical (shumariyati) tareeqe istemal ho sakte hain (6.1).

book_ref.quote: This large number allows for the use of statistical methods

blocks.prompt:
9 The average kinetic energy of gas particles is directly proportional to the:
(Gas ke zarraat ki average kinetic energy kis ke barah-e-raast mutanasib (directly proportional) hai?)
blocks.explanation: Mafrooza 6: average kinetic energy gas ke absolute (kelvin) temperature ke barah-e-raast mutanasib hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: directly proportional to the absolute temperature of the gas

blocks.prompt:
10 When the temperature of a gas is increased, the speed of its particles:
(Jab gas ka temperature barhaya jaye to us ke zarraat ki speed:)
blocks.explanation: Temperature barhne se average kinetic energy aur is liye zarraat ki speed barhti hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: as the temperature increases, the speed of the gas particles also increases

blocks.prompt:
11 The pressure exerted by a gas on the walls of its container is due to:
(Gas apne bartan ki deewaron par jo pressure dalti hai woh kis wajah se hai?)

options.text: gas molecules ki aapas mein kashish
gas ke zarraat ki deewaron se takkar

blocks.explanation: Pressure gas ke zarraat ki deewaron se takkar ki wajah se hai; takkar ke waqt ki force pressure paida karti hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: is due to the collisions of gas particles with the walls

blocks.prompt:
12 In the kinetic theory, the time taken for a collision is:
(Kinetic theory mein aik takkar mein lagne wala waqt:)

options.text: do takkaron ke darmiyani waqt ke muqable mein intehai kam

blocks.explanation: Takkar ka waqt do takkaron ke darmiyani waqt ke muqable mein intehai kam hai; is se tajziya aasaan ho jata hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: extremely short compared to the time between collisions

blocks.prompt:
13 Real gases deviate most from the assumptions of the kinetic theory at:
(Real gases kinetic theory ke mafroozat se sab se zyada kab hat-ti (deviate karti) hain?)

options.text: sirf khala mein kam pressure aur kam temperature
bohat zyada temperature par koi bhi pressure

blocks.explanation: Real gases intermolecular forces aur molecules ke mehdood volume ki wajah se, khaas taur par zyada pressure aur kam temperature par, hat-ti hain (6.1).

book_ref.quote: especially at high pressures and low temperatures

blocks.prompt:
14 Real gases deviate from ideal behaviour because of:
(Real gases ideal rawayye se kyun hat-ti hain?)

options.text: intermolecular forces aur molecules ka mehdood volume

blocks.explanation: Yeh farq intermolecular forces (molecules ke darmiyan quwwatein) aur molecules ke mehdood volume ki wajah se hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: real gases exhibit deviations due to intermolecular forces and finite molecular volume

blocks.prompt:
15 A gas that obeys the kinetic theory of gases is called:
(Jo gas kinetic theory of gases ki pairwi kare use kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Jo gas kinetic theory ki pairwi kare use ideal (misali) gas kehte hain (6.1).

book_ref.quote: A gas that obeys kinetic theory of gases is termed as an ideal gas

blocks.prompt:
16 The value of the universal gas constant R used in the chapter is:
(Chapter mein universal gas constant R ki qeemat kya di gayi hai?)
blocks.explanation: R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (6.1); 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ k_B hai aur 6.02 × 10²³ Nₐ hai.

book_ref.quote: R is universal gas constant (R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

blocks.prompt:
17 For a fixed amount of an ideal gas, PV = nRT shows that the product PV is directly proportional to:
(Ideal gas ki muqarrara miqdaar ke liye PV = nRT batati hai ke PV kis ke barah-e-raast mutanasib hai?)
blocks.explanation: Equation (6.1) ke mutabiq PV temperature ke barah-e-raast mutanasib hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: product of pressure and volume is directly proportional to the temperature

blocks.prompt:
18 Two moles of an ideal gas at 300 K occupy 0.050 m³. Using R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, its pressure is about:
(Ideal gas ke 2 moles 300 K par 0.050 m³ gherte hain. R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ le kar us ka pressure taqreeban kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: Here P represents pressure, V is volume, n is number of moles

blocks.prompt:
19 The Boltzmann constant k_B is defined as:
(Boltzmann constant k_B ki definition kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: R/Nₐ ko Boltzmann constant kehte hain: k_B = R/Nₐ (Eq. 6.2).

book_ref.quote: The term R/Nₐ is termed as Boltzmann constant k_B.

blocks.prompt:
20 The value of the Boltzmann constant is:
(Boltzmann constant ki qeemat kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: Substituting the values of R and Nₐ, we have

blocks.prompt:
21 In terms of the Boltzmann constant, the ideal gas equation is:
(Boltzmann constant ki shakal mein ideal gas equation kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: PV = (N/Nₐ)RT mein k_B = R/Nₐ rakhne se PV = N k_B T (Eq. 6.3) milti hai; N molecules ki tadaad hai.

book_ref.quote: Equation (6.3) gives ideal gas equation in terms of Boltzmann constant.

blocks.prompt:
22 A sample of gas contains 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules. Taking Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³, the number of moles is:
(Gas ke aik namoone mein 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules hain. Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³ le kar moles ki tadaad kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: It can be defined as the number of atoms are molecules per unit Avogadro's number

blocks.prompt:
23 A gas at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K occupies 1.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, the number of molecules is about:
(Aik gas 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa aur 300 K par 1.0 × 10⁻³ m³ gherti hai. k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ le kar molecules ki tadaad taqreeban kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: Substituting Eq. (6.2) in Eq. (iii),

blocks.prompt:
24 Real gases approach ideal behaviour under:
(Real gases kin halaat mein ideal rawayye ke qareeb aati hain?)
blocks.explanation: Real gases kam pressure aur zyada temperature par ideal rawayye ke qareeb aati hain (6.1).

book_ref.quote: Real gases approach ideal behaviour under: (i) low pressure (ii) high temperature

blocks.prompt:
25 For a real gas behaving like an ideal gas, the energy of its molecules is:
(Jab real gas ideal gas ki tarah rawayya rakhe to us ke molecules ki energy:)
blocks.explanation: Jab intermolecular forces na-qabil-e-lehaaz hon to molecules ki P.E. na hone ke barabar hai aur sirf K.E. hoti hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: P.E. of the gas molecules is negligible and this have only K.E.

blocks.prompt:
26 The density of an ideal gas of molar mass M at pressure P and temperature T is given by:
(Molar mass M wali ideal gas ki pressure P aur temperature T par density kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: n = m/M rakhne se PV = (m/M)RT, yani PM = (m/V)RT, is liye ρ = PM/RT (6.1).

book_ref.quote: In Eq. (6.1) n represents number of moles which can be given by

blocks.prompt:
27 At low pressure and high temperature, the density of a gas is:
(Kam pressure aur zyada temperature par gas ki density:)

options.text: zyada, is liye molecules qareeb qareeb
kam, is liye molecules door door

blocks.explanation: Chunke ρ ∝ P/T, kam pressure aur zyada temperature par density kam hai; molecules door door hote hain aur forces na hone ke barabar (6.1).

book_ref.quote: The density of a gas will be low at low pressure and high temperature

blocks.prompt:
28 Oxygen (M = 0.032 kg mol⁻¹) is at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K. Treating it as an ideal gas (R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), its density is about:
(Oxygen (M = 0.032 kg mol⁻¹) 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa aur 300 K par hai. Ise ideal gas maan kar (R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) us ki density taqreeban kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: So, the real gas behaves like an ideal gas at low pressure and high temperature.

blocks.prompt:
29 If the pressure of an ideal gas is kept constant and its kelvin temperature is doubled, its density becomes:
(Agar ideal gas ka pressure sabit rakha jaye aur kelvin temperature dugna kar diya jaye to us ki density:)
blocks.explanation: ρ ∝ P/T; sabit P par T dugna karne se density aadhi ho jaati hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: the intermolecular forces will be negligible

blocks.prompt:
30 The laws relating pressure, volume and temperature of an ideal gas, with one variable kept constant, are called:
(Ideal gas ke pressure, volume aur temperature ko (aik ko sabit rakh kar) aapas mein jorne wale qawaneen kya kehlate hain?)
blocks.explanation: Ideal gas ke P, V aur T ko aapas mein jorne wale qawaneen gas laws kehlate hain (6.1).

book_ref.quote: The laws that relate these variables mutually for an ideal gas are termed as gas laws.

blocks.prompt:
31 Boyle's law relates the pressure and volume of a fixed mass of gas at constant:
(Boyle's law gas ki muqarrara miqdaar ke pressure aur volume ko kis cheez ke sabit hone par jorta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Boyle's law sabit temperature par gas ke P aur V ka taalluq deta hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: provides a relationship between pressure and volume of a gas at constant temperature

blocks.prompt:
32 Boyle's law was introduced by Robert Boyle in the year:
(Robert Boyle ne Boyle's law kis saal pesh kiya?)
blocks.explanation: Robert Boyle ne yeh qanoon 1662 mein pesh kiya (6.1). 1824 Carnot ka engine aur 1856 Clausius ki entropy hai.

book_ref.quote: This law was introduced by Robert Boyle in 1662

blocks.prompt:
33 A fixed mass of gas occupies 9.0 L at 2.0 atm. At constant temperature its pressure is raised to 3.0 atm. Its new volume is:
(Gas ki muqarrara miqdaar 2.0 atm par 9.0 L gherti hai. Sabit temperature par pressure 3.0 atm kar diya jaye to naya volume kya hoga?)
blocks.explanation: Boyle's law: V₂ = P₁V₁/P₂ = 2.0 × 9.0/3.0 = 6.0 L (6.1).

book_ref.quote: pressure P exerted by a gas varies inversely with volume V

blocks.prompt:
34 A gas at 100 kPa is compressed at constant temperature from 4.0 L to 2.5 L. Its pressure becomes:
(100 kPa wali gas sabit temperature par 4.0 L se 2.5 L tak dabayi jaati hai. Us ka pressure kitna ho jata hai?)

book_ref.quote: It is sated that for a fixed mass of an ideal gas

blocks.prompt:
35 At constant temperature, a graph of pressure P against volume V for a fixed mass of gas is:
(Sabit temperature par gas ki muqarrara miqdaar ke liye pressure P aur volume V ka graph kaisa hota hai?)

options.text: aik curve jis mein V barhne par P kam hota hai
origin se guzarti seedhi lakeer jis ki dhalwan musbat

blocks.explanation: Boyle's law: P ∝ 1/V, is liye V barhne par P kam hota hai aur graph aik curve hai (Fig. 6.1).

book_ref.quote: Boyle's law is shown graphically in Fig. 6.1.

blocks.prompt:
36 Charles' law relates the volume and temperature of a fixed mass of gas at constant:
(Charles' law gas ki muqarrara miqdaar ke volume aur temperature ko kis cheez ke sabit hone par jorta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Charles' law sabit pressure par gas ke V aur T ko jorta hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: Charles' law relates volume and temperature of an ideal gas for a fixed mass at constant pressure.

blocks.prompt:
37 Jacques Charles found the law that bears his name in about:
(Jacques Charles ne apne naam wala qanoon taqreeban kab daryaft kiya?)
blocks.explanation: Kitab ki 'Book correction' ke mutabiq taqreeban 1787 (Gay-Lussac ne 1802 mein shaya kiya); chhapa hua 1870 ghalat hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: Jacques Charles (1746–1823) found this law in about 1787

blocks.prompt:
38 A gas occupies 300 mL at 27 °C. At constant pressure it is heated to 127 °C. Its new volume is:
(Aik gas 27 °C par 300 mL gherti hai. Sabit pressure par use 127 °C tak garam kiya jata hai. Naya volume kya hoga?)
blocks.explanation: T₁ = 300 K, T₂ = 400 K; V₂ = V₁T₂/T₁ = 300 × 400/300 = 400 mL. Kelvin temperature lazmi hai (6.1).

book_ref.quote: the volume of given mass of gas at constant pressure is directly proportional to the absolute temperature

blocks.prompt:
39 A graph of volume V against absolute temperature T for a gas at constant pressure is:
(Sabit pressure par gas ke volume V aur absolute temperature T ka graph kaisa hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Sabit pressure par V ∝ T, is liye V-T graph origin se guzarti seedhi lakeer hai (Fig. 6.2).

book_ref.quote: Graphically, it can be shown in Fig. 6.2.

blocks.prompt:
40 Gay-Lussac's law states that, at constant volume, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas varies:
(Gay-Lussac's law ke mutabiq sabit volume par gas ki muqarrara miqdaar ka pressure:)
blocks.explanation: Gay-Lussac's law: sabit volume par P ∝ T (6.1).

book_ref.quote: the pressure exerted by a gas varies directly with absolute temperature of the gas at constant volume

blocks.prompt:
41 A gas in a closed rigid container is at 150 kPa and 300 K. If it is heated to 400 K, its pressure becomes:
(Band sakht bartan mein gas 150 kPa aur 300 K par hai. Use 400 K tak garam karne par pressure kitna hoga?)
blocks.explanation: P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 150 × 400/300 = 200 kPa (Gay-Lussac's law, 6.1).

book_ref.quote: Graphically, Gay-Lussac's law is shown in Fig. 6.3.

blocks.prompt:
42 Two bodies in thermal contact are in thermal equilibrium when they have the same:
(Do jism jo thermal contact mein hon, kab thermal equilibrium mein hote hain?)
blocks.explanation: Barabar temperature par heat ke bahao ki koi wajah nahi hoti, is liye jism thermal equilibrium mein rehte hain (6.1).

book_ref.quote: there is no driving force for heat transfer between them

blocks.prompt:
43 A metal spoon is put into hot coffee. When thermal equilibrium is reached:
(Garam coffee mein dhaat ka chamach rakha jata hai. Jab thermal equilibrium ho jaye to:)

options.text: heat coffee se chamach ki taraf behti rehti hai
chamach coffee se zyada garam ho jata hai
un ke darmiyan heat ka koi kul bahao nahi
heat chamach se coffee ki taraf behti hai

blocks.explanation: Aakhir coffee aur chamach ka temperature barabar ho jata hai; phir heat ka koi kul bahao nahi hota (6.1).

book_ref.quote: there is no net heat flow between the coffee and the spoon

blocks.prompt:
44 The internal energy of a substance is the sum of:
(Kisi maadde ki internal energy kis ka majmooa hai?)

options.text: di gayi heat aur kiya gaya work
molecules ki tamam kinetic aur potential energies

blocks.explanation: Internal energy (androoni tawanai) molecules ki tamam kinetic aur potential energies ka majmooa hai (6.2).

book_ref.quote: The sum of all forms of molecular energies (kinetic and potential) of a substance

blocks.prompt:
45 The internal energy of an ideal gas is generally the:
(Ideal gas ki internal energy aam taur par kya hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Ideal gas ke molecules mass points hain jo koi force nahi lagate, is liye internal energy un ki translational (seedhi harkat wali) K.E. hai (6.2).

book_ref.quote: the internal energy of an ideal gas system is generally the translational K.E. of its molecules

blocks.prompt:
46 For an ideal gas system, internal energy is:
(Ideal gas system ke liye internal energy:)
blocks.explanation: Ideal gas ke liye internal energy us ke temperature ke barah-e-raast mutanasib hai (6.2).

book_ref.quote: the internal energy is directly proportional to its temperature

blocks.prompt:
47 Besides translational and rotational energy, a diatomic gas molecule also has:
(Translational aur rotational energy ke ilawa diatomic gas molecule mein aur kaun si energy hoti hai?)

options.text: spring jaise bond ki vibrational energy

blocks.explanation: Diatomic molecule mein atoms ke darmiyan spring jaise bond ki vibrational (thartharahat wali) energy bhi hoti hai (6.2).

book_ref.quote: It also has vibrational energy associated with the spring like bond between its atoms.

blocks.prompt:
48 According to the kinetic theory, the average kinetic energy of a gas molecule at absolute temperature T is:
(Kinetic theory ke mutabiq absolute temperature T par gas molecule ki average kinetic energy kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: According to the kinetic theory of gases, the average kinetic energy of gas molecules is given by

blocks.prompt:
49 Using k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, the average kinetic energy of a gas molecule at 400 K is:
(k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ le kar 400 K par gas molecule ki average kinetic energy kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: where k_B is Boltzmann constant.

blocks.prompt:
50 The kelvin temperature of an ideal gas is raised from 300 K to 600 K. The average kinetic energy of its molecules becomes:
(Ideal gas ka kelvin temperature 300 K se 600 K kiya jata hai. Molecules ki average kinetic energy kitni ho jaati hai?)
blocks.explanation: Average K.E. = (3/2) k_B T ∝ T; T dugna karne se average K.E. dugni ho jaati hai (6.2).

book_ref.quote: the rise in temperature of an object reflects an increase in the internal kinetic energy

blocks.prompt:
51 During a phase change such as melting, the heat supplied:
(Phase ki tabdeeli (maslan pighalne) ke dauran di gayi heat:)

options.text: temperature badle baghair maadde ki halat badalti hai
saari work mein badal jaati hai

blocks.explanation: Phase ki tabdeeli mein heat maadde ki halat badalti hai, temperature nahi badalta (6.2).

book_ref.quote: phase changes (where heat energy changes the state of matter without changing temperature)

blocks.prompt:
52 Internal energy is a function of state. This means it:
(Internal energy state ka function hai. Is ka matlab hai ke yeh:)

options.text: ikhtiyar kiye gaye raaste par munhasir
sirf ibtidai aur aakhri halat par munhasir, raaste par nahi
mukammal (absolute) taur par napi ja sakti hai

blocks.explanation: State function hone ki wajah se internal energy raaste par nahi, sirf ibtidai aur aakhri halat par munhasir hai; sirf us ki tabdeeli aham hai (6.2).

book_ref.quote: Internal energy is a function of state.

blocks.prompt:
53 Internal energy is similar to gravitational potential energy in that:
(Internal energy gravitational potential energy se kis lehaaz se milti julti hai?)

options.text: sirf us ki tabdeeli aham hai, mukammal qeemat nahi

blocks.explanation: P.E. ki tarah internal energy ki bhi sirf tabdeeli aham hai, mukammal qeemat nahi (6.2).

book_ref.quote: Thus, internal energy is similar to the gravitational P.E.

blocks.prompt:
54 According to the sign convention of the chapter, work done by the system on its environment is taken as:
(Chapter ke sign convention ke mutabiq system ka apne mahaul par kiya gaya work kaisa liya jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Andar aane wali heat aur bahar nikalne wala work musbat hain: system ka kiya work musbat, us par kiya work manfi (6.3).

book_ref.quote: work done by the system on its environment is considered positive

blocks.prompt:
55 When the surroundings compress a gas, the work W in the first law is:
(Jab mahaul gas ko dabata hai to first law mein work W kaisa hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Mahaul ka system par kiya gaya work manfi liya jata hai (6.3).

book_ref.quote: work done on the system by the environment is taken as negative

blocks.prompt:
56 Heat in and work out were defined as positive because the idea was first applied to the:
(Andar aane wali heat aur bahar nikalne wala work musbat kyun maane gaye? Kyunke yeh khayal pehli baar kis par laagu hua:)
blocks.explanation: Steam engine mein heat andar de kar work bahar lena qudrati tha, is liye dono musbat liye gaye (6.3).

book_ref.quote: The idea was first applied to the steam engine

blocks.prompt:
57 A gas at pressure P pushes a frictionless piston of area A. The force on the piston is:
(Pressure P wali gas area A wale be-ragar piston ko dhakelti hai. Piston par force kitni hai?)
blocks.explanation: Gas ki piston par force F = PA hai (6.3).

book_ref.quote: The force F exerted by the gas on the piston is PA.

blocks.prompt:
58 In deriving W = PΔV, the gas is assumed to expand very slowly so that it:
(W = PΔV nikalte waqt farz kiya jata hai ke gas bohat aahista phailti hai taake:)

options.text: absolute zero tak thandi ho jaye

blocks.explanation: Gas ΔV tak bohat aahista phailti hai taake woh equilibrium (tawazun) mein rahe (6.3).

book_ref.quote: We assume that the gas expands through ΔV very slowly

blocks.prompt:
59 A gas expands against a constant pressure of 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa and its volume increases by 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³. The work done by the gas is:
(Aik gas 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa ke sabit pressure par phailti hai aur us ka volume 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ barhta hai. Gas ka kiya gaya work kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: the work W done by the gas is:

blocks.prompt:
60 Gas at 5000 N m⁻² pushes a piston of area 0.20 m² up through 5.0 cm at constant pressure. The work done by the gas is:
(5000 N m⁻² wali gas 0.20 m² area wale piston ko sabit pressure par 5.0 cm upar dhakelti hai. Gas ka work kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: As the piston moves up through a small distance Δy

blocks.prompt:
61 On a P-V graph, the work done by a gas is equal to the:
(P-V graph par gas ka kiya gaya work kis ke barabar hai?)

options.text: P-V curve ke neeche ka area

blocks.explanation: Work P-V graph ke neeche wale area ke barabar hai (Fig. 6.5).

book_ref.quote: The work done can also be calculated by area of the curve under P-V graph

blocks.prompt:
62 The general principles dealing with heat energy and its transformation into mechanical energy are called:
(Heat energy aur us ki mechanical energy mein tabdeeli se mutaliq aam usool kya kehlate hain?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh usool thermodynamics ke qawaneen kehlate hain (6.3).

book_ref.quote: These principles are known as laws of thermodynamics.

blocks.prompt:
63 The first law of thermodynamics is written as:
